# Árgos: the restoration, the temple, and the world it opens
Every name in this series was once flattened to fit a keyboard. **Árgos** is what the evidence put back.

Árgos exists within a single great story — the wanderings of Io — but it is one of the oldest stories the Greeks told, already old when Homer gave Hermês the epithet Argeiphontēs, 'Slayer of Árgos'. Zeús loved Io, daughter of the river-god Inachos, and to hide her from Hera — so the common telling runs — she was changed into a white cow.  Hera was not deceived.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Árgos
- **ASCII form:** argos
- **Meaning:** "Shining, swift"
- **Domain of influence:** Vigilance, Hera's Watcher
- **Pantheon:** Greek
- **Classification:** Tier 2
- **Original script:** Ἄργος
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 31 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

The name is attested as **Ἄργος**. On the evidence, it means "Shining, swift".

Strip **Árgos** to *argos* and one piece of evidence vanishes:

- **a → Á** — Acute on a: the stress position the ASCII form cannot show.

A reader who knows the marks hears the name correctly on the first try. A reader who never sees them never gets the chance.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Árgos** lives at [/sites/argos/](/sites/argos/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/argos/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/argos/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/argos/patterns/).

The restoration preserves one decisive feature the ASCII form drops — a single, honest mark — which places it in Tier-2: exact, and exactly labeled.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Árgos** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Cybersecurity & Digital Protection** — The hundred eyes that never close — total monitoring, zero blind spots.
- **Defense, Military & Security** — Hera's appointed watchman over Io — guard duty personified.
- **Optics, Imaging & Vision** — A hundred eyes covering every angle — vision itself as a brand.

The mapping is conservative on purpose: only resonances that can be argued aloud. The rest of the atlas follows the same rule, industry by industry.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Greek tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Theogony](/texts/theogony/), [Homeric Hymns](/texts/homeric-hymns/), and [Works and Days](/texts/works-and-days/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
## The File Continues

This is one of 271 Restoration Files — a second dispatch from every flagship temple in the fleet. The temple's [first dispatch](/sites/argos/blog/) tells the founding story of the name; the [blog index](/blog/) holds the whole archive.
